doc: Work in progress. From a topological_offset construction (a .vtu, or a .msh with corr_input_vid), thins the offset band around the solid to a target thickness and, with prism_dominant, rebuilds it as prisms, pyramids and tets.

Enable rod preparation within the shared shell/rod optimizer. Accepts mixed curve, face and solid offset constructions. Rod edges are input edges without input face/solid cofaces. Non-rod attachments and branching joints protect one-rings; free ends use terminal frames, and isolated loops reuse a periodic frame without endpoint protection. Build rod frame targets and shell normal targets, then jointly collapse/smooth with the complete background and reconstruct both kinds of prism plus conforming pyramid/tet interfaces. Requires explicit input labels and correspondence. The isolated corner-preview experiment remains curve-only.
Rod mode only. Absolute target section radius; positive, or zero to use thicknessratio times the mean centerline edge length. Infeasible circular targets retain valid geometry and are reported.
Rod mode only. Insert a midpoint input vertex and equivalent frame into compatible prism intervals during construction; both halves and all changed background interfaces must validate before commit.

Experimental rod-mode local patch export. A nonnegative input source vid constructs a quaternion-interpolated corner buffer, fixing its local pose and the two neighboring section interfaces. Exports only the isolated patch; does not replace or include the source background. -1 keeps the normal full-mesh pipeline. Requires prism_dominant.
For rod_corner_preview_vid only. Maximum quaternion rotation between adjacent buffer frames, in degrees, in (0,90]. The corner pose stays fixed; extra frames lie on the original two input segments.

For rod_corner_preview_vid only. Maximum additional binary subdivision depth in [0,7]. Try the initial interpolated buffer, then double both side layer counts on each failed geometric attempt. If no valid prism construction is found within this bound, export the unchanged local reference tets. A separate 128-layer-per-side bound limits work.
Application name must be prismatic_mesh.
Construction .vtu or Gmsh 4.1 .msh with corr_input_vid. MSH can derive labels and cell tags from the tag_0/offset/ambient physical groups; explicit PRISM fields are also supported.
Output .vtu or .msh (Gmsh 4.1 ASCII) filename, relative to the JSON directory. A missing extension becomes .vtu.
Base directory for input; set by wmtk_app to the JSON directory.
Positive target thickness relative to the mean length of unique input surface edges.
Number of collapse/smoothing iterations; 0 computes targets without optimization.

Keep exterior background tetrahedra during optimization/output. Background must remain strictly positive. Without background_remeshing only offset vertices move. Targets are computed from the band alone.

Explicitly discard background tetrahedra before rod preprocessing and joint optimization. Keep input volume and offset band, remove background constraints and background-pyramid reconstruction, and do not reattach the discarded mesh. Overrides keep_background_mesh. Intended for a band-only result or a background-constraint comparison.

After optimization, reconstruct conforming prisms, input-apex shell pyramids and tetrahedra. Retained background receives kernel-point pyramids in feasible disjoint quad-diagonal edge-star cavities. Preserve existing points, input volume and non-cavity background; fall back to conforming tet regions on failed geometry, overlap or search limits.
Additionally export the union of input volume and offset band as <output_stem>_input_shell.msh and .vtu, using the same final coordinates, hybrid cells and attributes while omitting background cells.

Optional nonnegative signed-volume floor for new or modified shell tetrahedra, candidate pyramid decompositions and new background pyramid cavity cones. The default zero requires strictly positive volume using exact predicates, without a coordinate-scale-dependent cutoff. Background optimization and unchanged background tets also require strictly positive volume.
Maximum smoothing step halvings after the full target step; between 0 and 60.
Optional prism Jacobian smoothing rounds after tet optimization. Zero disables this stage. Only offset vertices move; input, correspondence and connectivity remain fixed.

Optional fraction in [0,1). Each collapse or smoothing move must retain more than this fraction of every modified surviving tet's volume, including background. Zero keeps the original strict-positive rule. Deleted collapse cells are excluded. The absolute band min_tet_volume floor still applies.

Optional local convex-envelope initialization and concave-hinge smoothing after hybrid construction, in [0,100]. Only outer offset vertices in protected/marked transition neighborhoods move. Input, correspondence, connectivity and completed rod-prism frames stay fixed; every step checks reference tets, native prism/pyramid Jacobians and native shape quality. Zero disables this stage.
Positive target det(J), normalized by twice input triangle area times initial mean column length.
Positive quadratic weight on displacement from the position before Jacobian smoothing, normalized by target thickness (initial column length if unavailable).
Positive per-move displacement bound relative to thickness. Implemented with an inscribed axis-aligned box.
Positive total displacement bound from the position before Jacobian smoothing, relative to thickness. Implemented with an inscribed axis-aligned box.

Enable adaptive background 2-3/3-2 swaps and interior relaxation after each tet iteration, then retry collapse. Requires keep_background_mesh=true. Input/offset vertices and exterior boundary are fixed during remeshing.
Local remeshing passes per tet iteration; positive.
Trigger on background mean ratio below this threshold in (0,1]; 1 is a regular tet, 0 is degenerate. Background-blocked collapses are also repair targets.
Maximum accepted background swaps/moves per tet iteration; positive.
Maximum attempted background swaps/moves per tet iteration; positive.
